description.narrative:
Supporting Displaced and Repatriated Populations in the Border Communes of Cornillon and Belladère, Haiti – Year 3 of the SCLR Project In 2024, the border communes of Cornillon and Belladère have become key host communities for two vulnerable groups: migrants forcibly repatriated from the Dominican Republic and internally displaced persons (IDPs) fleeing violence perpetrated by armed groups in the capital, Port-au-Prince. Among the most vulnerable are women, children, and persons with disabilities seeking to resettle in or near their communities of origin. These communes face serious structural and infrastructural challenges. The population of Cornillon and Belladère lives in extreme socio-economic vulnerability and struggles to meet basic needs such as access to clean water, healthcare, education, and food. Other pressing concerns include deteriorating road conditions and a general lack of public infrastructure—issues particularly acute in Cornillon. The mass arrival of repatriated migrants and displaced persons has further intensified the humanitarian crisis, requiring urgent and sustained attention. According to the GARR (Groupe d’Appui aux Rapatriés et Réfugiés), 18,334 repatriation cases were recorded in February 2025 alone. Of these, 12,236 occurred at the official border crossing point of Carrizal in Belladère. Meanwhile, Cornillon recorded 684 repatriations—6.73% of the total—through unofficial crossing points. In response, GARR will provide technical and financial support to grassroots community-based organisations in Cornillon and Belladère through Year 3 of the Supporting Community-Led Response (SCLR) project. A total of four grassroots organisations will each receive an average micro-grant of USD 2,500. Expected Results:
Strengthened capacities of local structures (CBOs, CSOs, self-help groups) and solidarity mutual groups (MUSO), particularly in the commune of Cornillon.
Direct improvement in living conditions for at least 500 people as a result of community-led interventions.
